Class PriceFreshnessService

java.lang.Object
grafioschtrader.service.PriceFreshnessService
@Service public class PriceFreshnessService extends Object
Measures how old the price of an instrument is, counted in trading sessions of the exchange it belongs to.

Counting calendar days would report every Monday morning as two days of delay and would turn a market wide holiday into an alarm, so the age is expressed in sessions the exchange really held. A price from the last completed session is current and yields zero, no matter how many days of weekend or holiday lie in between.

Currency pairs belong to no exchange. They are measured against the worldwide calendar alone, which is the closest thing to a session list a foreign exchange rate has.

  • Field Details

    • MAX_STALE_TRADING_SESSIONS

      public static final int MAX_STALE_TRADING_SESSIONS
      Highest age reported. Beyond it an instrument is simply stale; distinguishing forty from four hundred sessions carries no information for the user and would only stretch the colour ramp of the user interface.

      @Transactional(readOnly=true) public Map<Integer, List<LocalDate>> loadSessions(Collection<Integer> idsStockexchange, LocalDate today)

    • sessionsBehind

      public Integer sessionsBehind(List<LocalDate> sessionsDesc, LocalDate priceDate, LocalDate today)
      Counts the completed sessions that went by without the price being renewed.

      The current day itself is left out on purpose: a market that has not opened yet legitimately shows the price of the previous session, and reporting that as a delay would paint every instrument as stale each morning.

      Parameters:
      sessionsDesc - sessions of the exchange, newest first, as returned by loadSessions(Collection, LocalDate)
      priceDate - the day the displayed price belongs to, may be null
      today - the current day
      Returns:
      zero when the price is current, otherwise the number of missed sessions capped at MAX_STALE_TRADING_SESSIONS; null when the age cannot be told
